reference.title: Dumbbell LU Raise (male)
reference.listing: Page not read (gymvisual.com is blocked by the proxy); movement taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice.
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Breathe out on the way up, breathe in on the way down.
breathing.cadence: About 2 s up, short pause overhead, about 2.5 s down

prescription.load: Light dumbbells (lighter than a normal lateral raise)
prescription.progression: Add reps, then weight; pause at shoulder height on the way up

cues.text: Stand tall, feet hip width, knees soft. Dumbbells at the sides, palms in, arms straight with a soft elbow.
Breathe out and raise the arms out to the sides, turning the thumbs up as they pass shoulder height, and keep going until the dumbbells are overhead.
Arms long overhead, a little wider than the shoulders; ribs down, no lean back.
Breathe in and lower the same way, slowly, back to the sides.
Brief reset at the sides and repeat.

mistakes.mistake: Leaning back to get the dumbbells overhead
mistakes.fix: Brace the ribs down and squeeze the glutes; use lighter dumbbells.

mistakes.mistake: Bending the elbows into a press
mistakes.fix: Keep the arms long; the elbows stay soft but fixed.
Start each rep from a still position.

mistakes.mistake: Keeping the palms down past shoulder height
mistakes.fix: Turn the thumbs up as the arms pass shoulder height.

kinematics.norm: From the sides to overhead (about 160-170 degrees); the lateral raise loads the middle deltoid most (Coratella 2020; Campos 2020)
A little in front of the frontal plane (scapular plane) (clinical opinion)
Palms in at the sides, thumbs up from shoulder height (clinical opinion)
Slow, with a pause overhead (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #23695, Dumbbell LU Raise (male), video (movement reference only; page not read)
Coratella et al. 2020, an electromyographic analysis of lateral raise variations and frontal raise in competitive bodybuilders (Int J Environ Res Public Health 17(17):6015)
Campos et al. 2020, different shoulder exercises affect the activation of deltoid portions in resistance-trained individuals (J Hum Kinet 75:5-14)
Reinold et al. 2007, electromyographic analysis of the supraspinatus and deltoid muscles during 3 common rehabilitation exercises (J Athl Train 42(4):464-469)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, a pinching feeling in the front or top of the shoulder, numbness or tingling occurs.
The dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can control for every rep with good form.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Going overhead needs full, pain-free shoulder mobility; stop at shoulder height if it pinches.
Use much lighter dumbbells than for a normal lateral raise.
modify: Pinching overhead: stop at shoulder height (standard lateral raise).
Low-back arching: do it seated with the back supported.
regressions: Seated Lu raise with back support.
progressions: Pause at shoulder height on the way up and down.

muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_r: Prime mover through the whole arc; lateral raises gave the highest middle deltoid EMG among common shoulder exercises (Coratella 2020; Campos 2020).
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_l: Prime mover through the whole arc; lateral raises gave the highest middle deltoid EMG among common shoulder exercises (Coratella 2020; Campos 2020).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Helps above shoulder height, more as the arms come forward.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Helps above shoulder height, more as the arms come forward.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Upwardly rotates and lifts the shoulder blades to get the arms overhead.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Upwardly rotates and lifts the shoulder blades to get the arms overhead.
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Upwardly rotates the shoulder blades overhead.
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Upwardly rotates the shoulder blades overhead.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Turns the arms out (thumbs up) so they can pass overhead.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_l: Turns the arms out (thumbs up) so they can pass overhead.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the ribs down; no lean back.
